questions.q: In a scoped application, how is RESTMessageV2 typically referenced?
options: RESTMessageV2 directly, with no prefix
sn_ws.RESTMessageV2
gs.RESTMessageV2
sys_rest_message.RESTMessageV2
questions.explain: sn_ws.RESTMessageV2 is the real reference in a scoped application; Global scope can reference RESTMessageV2 directly without the namespace prefix.

questions.q:
What do the two arguments to the RESTMessageV2 constructor represent?

var r = new sn_ws.RESTMessageV2('WeatherAPI', 'getCurrentConditions');
options: The HTTP method and the Authentication Profile
The REST Message's name and the specific Function's name
The username and password for the external system
The base Endpoint and the relative path, written out directly
questions.explain: The constructor identifies which operation to call using exactly the two names configured earlier: the parent REST Message's name and the child Function's name.

questions.q: A Function's Endpoint is configured as /current?city=${city}. What is the correct script call to supply a real value for that placeholder?
options: r.setStringParameterNoEscape('city', 'Atlanta');
r.setEndpoint('city', 'Atlanta');
r.city = 'Atlanta';
r.execute('Atlanta');
questions.explain: setStringParameterNoEscape() substitutes a real value into a named ${placeholder} in the Function's Endpoint or Content, and must be called before execute().

options: execute() throws an exception, so the catch block runs
execute() still returns a response object; httpStatus is set to 500, and the catch block does not run
ServiceNow automatically retries the call three times before failing
The script stops immediately with no error handling at all
questions.explain: A server-side error status is still a completed HTTP exchange — execute() returns normally and getStatusCode() reflects the 500. Only a failure to complete the network call itself (DNS, timeout, unreachable host) throws.

questions.q: Why should .execute() always be wrapped in a try/catch?
options: Because JSON.parse() cannot run without it
Because setStringParameterNoEscape() requires it to function
Because a true network-level failure (unreachable host, DNS failure, timeout) causes execute() to throw an exception rather than return a response object
It isn't necessary — execute() never throws under any circumstance
questions.explain: A status-code check in an if statement only handles completed HTTP exchanges; a try/catch around execute() is what catches the case where the request never completed at all.
